column1: # Provenance of the AArch64 real-project reports (oss-report.py status
# --provenance; the format is in oss-report.py). Hand-kept from the lanes'
# state notes; it says what a report.json does not: the hod commit of a
# frozen copy named by its sha256, and the kiln of a report written before
# reports carried a `kiln` field. Update it with the lane when a lane
# kiln, gRPC (WP-211): the -O0 control on kiln 1.1.0; the -O0 hybrid build
# spans the switch to kiln 1.2.0 (kiln++ rebuilt in place at 01:19Z on
# 2026-11-15); the -O0 strict build and -O0 -g on kiln 1.2.0
# The third set (WP-211): OpenCV and CMake on kiln 1.2.0 in every tree (the
# rows at 02fe2d02 and the strict re-runs at cd6ef6bc); mold at hod 77873543
# frozen copies of the release candidates under other names (WP-211)
# The 15 projects of the hosted real-projects run 44078914310 of exactly
# a68a0d5d (GitHub's aarch64 runner, native; hod a68a0d5d built by the job,
# binary `hod`; kiln 8f93304ee): their reports carry no kiln commit

column2: zlib (the one stated exception of the lane rows, docs/RELEASE.md section 5): one of 37 objects, `infcover.c`, is compiled with `--coverage`, and kiln never offers such a translation unit to hod (skip reason `coverage`: the gcov instrumentation runs in kiln's LLVM pipeline), so 36 of 37 objects are hod's and the strict build is marked `failed`; the owner's decision of 2026-11-15: not hod's fault, does not block 1.0 (BACKLOG WP-279, coverage builds through hod). `infcover` does not link in either build (LLVM's profile runtime is absent on the lane host): 7 of 8 links and 5 of 6 tests, the control's.

duckdb -O0: the hybrid build is the one of hod 3b14f8ff, which declined one jemalloc translation unit as `alwaysinline:stacksave-escapes` (built since WP-237); it was not built again for this page. The strict build at a68a0d5d has 1901 of 1901 objects by hod.

duckdb -O0 -g: `test/sql/index/art/scan/test_random_uuid.test` failed in the hybrid build's test run (hod 56a4695f; not built again for this page) with an allocation failure under the 16 GB address-space cap, twice (in the -O0 hybrid run as well); run alone under the same cap it passes (reruns in the -O0 tree). The strict builds at a68a0d5d pass it: their results equal the control's case by case.

duckdb: the strict cells read 506/509 because a `unittest` child of `test_remote_optimizer.cpp` outlives the run and, when the lane kills it, its own Catch2 summary lands last in `test.log`, where the report takes its count. The per-case results are complete, 4,629 cases in each flavour: 4,614 pass and 15 fail, the control's 15, which is what the column "against the control" compares.

gRPC (WP-211): the rows have a strict build and no control cell: the control trees and reports were deleted for disk, so the generator has no control to compare with. The lane compares the strict builds program by program with the control's recorded results (CENSUS-3.md; kiln 8f93304ee for the `-O0 -g` control, kiln 21b9110a4 (1.1.0) for the `-O0` control, built before the pin moved). At the candidate a68a0d5d both strict builds were run again (kiln 8f93304ee): `-O0` and `-O0 -g` each 2002 of 2002 objects by hod, 26 links, 19 of 24 test programs pass, and the same 5 fail as in every control (each asks for gRPC's port server, which the lane does not run).

CMake: every failing test of every tree, the control's included, fails in a sub-case with "Current working directory cannot be established." from the built cmake, a flake of the build volume, in a different RunCMake suite per tree (the lane's census, CENSUS-3.md "cmake"). `-O0` strict at a68a0d5d: 97/97 (control 96/97). `-O0 -g` strict at a68a0d5d: 96/97 against the control's 96/97, `RunCMake.cmake_language` failing in both (in strict with the getcwd message). The hybrid builds are those of hod 02fe2d02, not built again for this page; their differences are the same flake in other suites.

mold: the three trees of each row were built on 2026-11-17 at kiln 8f93304ee (hybrid and strict with hod a68a0d5d) and run the same 1,362 tests. The same 360 fail in every tree, the control's included: 359 `i686-*` tests and `x86_64-arch-x86_64-empty-mergeable-section`. `-O0 -g` strict has one more in its full run, `x86_64-separate-debug-file-sort` (note above: it passed 3 of 3 reruns, and it passed in the hybrid build, where hod compiled the same 242 objects). The test links with `--separate-debug-file`, so mold's detached child writes `exe.dbg`; it waits with `flock exe.dbg true` and then reads the file with readelf. What was measured: on the lane's build volume the wait does not always hold while the writer has just created the file. A C program with no linker in it that repeats mold's calls (create, `flock`, write, `ftruncate`, write through a shared mapping) had its reader through before the writer finished in 40 of 40 runs on the volume and 0 of 40 on the container's own disk. The test's link with a larger input (20,000 functions) gave "Not an ELF file" after the lock in 15 of 150 runs with the hod-built mold and 4 of 150 with the control's mold on the volume, and 0 of 150 with each on the container's disk; strace shows the same calls on `exe.dbg` from both. The test's own small link repeated 1,600 times with the hod-built mold, and the `x86_64-s*` tests repeated 40 times each in the lane's shape with both, did not fail. Read as the volume's, not hod's; the difference between 15 and 4 of 150 is not explained.

benchmark, re2, abseil, googletest, fmt, protobuf, yaml_cpp, glog, nlohmann_json, doctest, spdlog, catch2, cli11, simdjson, leveldb: every tree of these rows (control, hybrid, strict) is from the hosted real-projects run 44078914310 (hod cell `a68a0d5d (hosted run 44078914310)`): built and tested natively on GitHub's aarch64 runner, hod a68a0d5d built by the job, kiln 8f93304ee.
